events.title: The Battle of Manzikert
events.shortBlurb: The Byzantine defeat that opened Asia Minor to the Turks and set the stage for the Crusades…
body: On 26 August 1071, near the town of Manzikert in Armenia, north of Lake Van, the army of the Byzantine emperor Romanus IV Diogenes met the Seljuk Turks under Sultan Alp Arslan, the 'Heroic Lion.' When the Turkish horse-archers wore down the imperial host and the reserve under Andronicus Doukas abandoned the field, the emperor's division was surrounded, and Romanus, wounded, was taken prisoner.

Alp Arslan treated his captive with honour and released him within days for a ransom, tribute, and a marriage alliance; but Constantinople had already acclaimed his stepson Michael VII, and Romanus, seized by his enemies, was blinded so savagely that he died of the ordeal in 1072. Alp Arslan himself outlived the battle by barely a year, stabbed by a condemned prisoner in November 1072.

The battle cost fewer lives than legend says, but its consequences were immense: with no army left to hold the frontier, Turkish tribes spread across Asia Minor, the ancient heartland of Eastern Christianity, taking Nicaea itself within a few years. The emperors' desperate appeals for Western aid helped move Pope Urban II, a generation later, to preach the First Crusade at Clermont in 1095.
